The '''2019 EFL Cup final''' was an [[association football]] match that took place on 24 February 2019 at [[Wembley Stadium]] in [[London]], England, to determine the winners of the [[2018–19 EFL Cup]].<ref name="EFLSchedule">{{cite web |title=Key Dates |url=https://www.efl.com/clubs-and-competitions/key-dates/ |publisher=[[English Football League]] |access-date=22 January 2019 }}</ref> It was contested by [[Chelsea F.C.|Chelsea]] and holders [[Manchester City F.C.|Manchester City]], who retained their title with a 4–3 victory on [[Penalty shoot-out (association football)|penalties]] following a 0–0 draw after extra time; it was the first time Manchester City had successfully defended a title. As winners, they would have entered the second qualifying round of the [[2019–20 UEFA Europa League]], but instead qualified directly for the [[2019–20 UEFA Champions League]] by finishing first in the [[2018–19 Premier League]]. The final was also a rematch of that season's [[2018 FA Community Shield|FA Community Shield]] which Manchester City won 2–0.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.mancity.com/citytv/match-highlights/2018/august/chelsea-v-man-city-community-shield-brief-match-highlights |title=CHELSEA V CITY: BRIEF HIGHLIGHTS |date=6 August 2018 |publisher=Manchester City FC |access-date=3 August 2019}}</ref>

Chelsea's participation in the [[2018–19 UEFA Europa League]] meant they entered the EFL Cup in the third round, where they were drawn away to fellow Premier League side [[Liverpool F.C.|Liverpool]]. After going behind, goals from [[Emerson Palmieri]] and [[Eden Hazard]] gave Chelsea a 2–1 win.<ref>{{cite news |first=Shamoon |last=Hafez |title=Liverpool 1–2 Chelsea |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/45569330 |publisher=BBC Sport |date=27 September 2018 |access-date=24 January 2019 }}</ref> In the next round, they were drawn at home to [[EFL Championship|Championship]] side [[Derby County F.C.|Derby County]]. This time, Chelsea took an early lead via a [[Fikayo Tomori]] own goal, but [[Jack Marriott (footballer)|Jack Marriott]] equalised for Derby four minutes later. Another own goal, this time by [[Richard Keogh]], put Chelsea ahead again in the 21st minute, only for [[Martyn Waghorn]] to level the scores six minutes later. Four minutes before half-time, [[Cesc Fàbregas]] scored what turned out to be the winning goal, as the second half went goalless.<ref>{{cite news |first=Emma |last=Sanders |title=Chelsea 3–2 Derby: Blues win dramatic Carabao Cup tie to reach last eight |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/45961339 |publisher=BBC Sport |date=31 October 2018 |access-date=24 January 2019 }}</ref>

In the fifth round, Chelsea were drawn at home to Premier League side [[A.F.C. Bournemouth|Bournemouth]], with Hazard again proving the difference between the two sides in a 1–0 win.<ref>{{cite news |first=Michael |last=Emons |title=Chelsea 1–0 Bournemouth: Eden Hazard goal sends Blues into semi-finals |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/46533821 |publisher=BBC Sport |date=19 December 2018 |access-date=24 January 2019 }}</ref> The semi-finals saw Chelsea drawn against [[Chelsea F.C.–Tottenham Hotspur F.C. rivalry|London rivals]] [[Tottenham Hotspur F.C.|Tottenham Hotspur]]. A [[Harry Kane]] penalty gave Tottenham a slim lead at Wembley Stadium in the first leg,<ref>{{cite news |first=Phil |last=McNulty |title=Tottenham 1–0 Chelsea, Carabao Cup – Harry Kane's penalty gives Spurs advantage |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/46726198 |publisher=BBC Sport |date=8 January 2019 |access-date=24 January 2019 }}</ref> but [[N'Golo Kanté]] levelled the aggregate scores after 27 minutes of the second leg. Hazard then put Chelsea in front with his third goal of the tournament in the 38th minute, only for [[Fernando Llorente]] to equalise again five minutes after half-time. The remainder of the match produced no further goals, and since the away goals rule was not in effect,<ref>{{cite news |title=No away goals rule tonight at Chelsea |url=https://www.tottenhamhotspur.com/news/2019/january/no-away-goals-rule-tonight-at-chelsea/ |website=tottenhamhotspur.com |publisher=Tottenham Hotspur FC |date=24 January 2019 |access-date=24 January 2019 }}</ref> the match went straight to a penalty shoot-out. Both sides converted their first two kicks each, before [[Eric Dier]] put his effort over the bar, allowing [[Jorginho (footballer, born December 1991)|Jorginho]] to give Chelsea the lead. [[Kepa Arrizabalaga]] then saved from [[Lucas Moura]], before [[David Luiz]] scored to send Chelsea to the final.<ref>{{cite news |first=Neil |last=Johnston |title=Carabao Cup: Chelsea 2–1 Tottenham (2–2 agg, Chelsea win 4–2 on pens) |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/46839114 |publisher=BBC Sport |date=24 January 2019 |access-date=24 January 2019 }}</ref>

Manchester City had qualified for the [[2018–19 UEFA Champions League]], and thus also entered the EFL Cup in the third round, drawn away to [[EFL League One|League One]] side [[Oxford United F.C.|Oxford United]]. At the [[Kassam Stadium]], Manchester City won 3–0 with goals from [[Gabriel Jesus]], [[Riyad Mahrez]] and [[Phil Foden]].<ref>{{cite news |first=Phil |last=McNulty |title=Oxford United 0-3 Manchester City: Carabao Cup holders see off League One strugglers |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/45555893 |publisher=BBC Sport |date=25 September 2018 |access-date=23 January 2019 }}</ref> In the fourth round, they were drawn with fellow Premier League club [[Fulham F.C.|Fulham]] at home. At their [[City of Manchester Stadium]], Manchester City won 2–0 via two goals from [[Brahim Díaz]].<ref>{{cite news |first=Chris |last=Bevan |title=Carabao Cup: Man City beat Fulham 2–0 to reach quarter-finals |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/45973796 |publisher=BBC Sport |date=1 November 2018 |access-date=23 January 2019 }}</ref> In the next round, they were drawn away at fellow Premier League side [[Leicester City F.C.|Leicester City]]. The match finished 1–1 at the [[King Power Stadium]], with [[Marc Albrighton]]'s 73rd-minute goal – the only one Manchester City conceded en route to the final – cancelling out [[Kevin De Bruyne]]'s early strike, but Manchester City won the resulting [[penalty shoot-out (association football)|penalty shoot-out]] 3–1 and progressed.<ref>{{cite news |first=Shamoon |last=Hafez |title=Leicester City 1–1 Manchester City (1–3 pens) |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/46516343 |publisher=BBC Sport |date=18 December 2018 |access-date=23 January 2019 }}</ref>

In the two legged semi-final, Manchester City drew League One side [[Burton Albion F.C.|Burton Albion]]. Manchester City won the first leg at the City of Manchester Stadium 9–0 in their biggest win for 31 years, with four goals from Jesus and one each from [[Kevin De Bruyne]], [[Oleksandr Zinchenko (footballer)|Oleksandr Zinchenko]], Foden, [[Kyle Walker]] and Mahrez.<ref>{{cite news |first=Michael |last=Emons |title=Manchester City 9–0 Burton Albion: Gabriel Jesus scores four in Carabao Cup semi-final |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/46732982 |publisher=BBC Sport |date=9 January 2019 |access-date=23 January 2019 }}</ref> In the second leg at the [[Pirelli Stadium]], [[Sergio Agüero]] scored his first goal of the competition to give Manchester City a 1–0 win (10–0 on aggregate) and confirm their place in the final.<ref>{{cite news |first=Emlyn |last=Begley |title=Manchester City reach Carabao Cup final with 10–0 aggregate win over Burton Albion |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/46839107 |publisher=BBC Sport |date=23 January 2019 |access-date=23 January 2019 }}</ref>
{{Clear}}

==Pre-match==
Manchester City boss [[Pep Guardiola]] was thinking of playing second choice [[goalkeeper (association football)|goalkeeper]] [[Arijanet Muric]] instead of [[Ederson Moraes|Ederson]] as Muric had played for the duration of City's route to the final and conceded just once. He left Muric sweating about his place by insisting that he would make a lot call on whether to play him or not.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://metro.co.uk/2019/02/24/pep-guardiola-ready-to-keep-faith-in-arijanet-muric-ahead-of-ederson-for-carabao-cup-final-8722497/|title=Pep Guardiola ready to keep faith in Arijanet Muric ahead of Ederson for Carabao Cup final|last=Kearns|first=Sean|date=24 February 2019|website=Metro|access-date=26 February 2019}}</ref>

==Match==

===Summary===
The match was overshadowed by an incident near the end of extra time, with the score at 0–0 and a penalty shoot-out looming, that saw Chelsea goalkeeper [[Kepa Arrizabalaga]] defy manager [[Maurizio Sarri]] and refuse to be substituted for [[Willy Caballero]] (whose penalty saves won former club Manchester City the [[2016 Football League Cup final]]). Arrizabalaga ultimately stayed on the pitch, while an irate Sarri nearly stormed into the match tunnel, and was later held back by Chelsea player [[Antonio Rüdiger]] from confronting Arrizabalaga.<ref name=telegraphlive>{{cite web |last1=Burt |first1=Jason |last2=Tyers |first2=Mike |title=Manchester City take the honours after Kepa Arrizabalaga antics overshadow otherwise drab League Cup final |url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/football/2019/02/24/chelsea-vs-manchester-city-carabao-cup-final-2019-live-score/ |work=[[The Daily Telegraph]] |access-date=25 February 2019}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last1=Bhardwaj |first1=Vaishali |title=Man City beat Chelsea to win EFL Cup Final after Wembley penalty shootout |url=https://www.standard.co.uk/sport/football/chelsea-vs-man-city-efl-cup-final-report-result-wembley-a4075136.html |work=[[Evening Standard]] |access-date=25 February 2019}}</ref>

The shoot-out, taken at the Chelsea fans' end, saw Chelsea starting: Jorginho's low, weak shot was saved by City goalkeeper [[Ederson Moraes|Ederson]], while [[İlkay Gündoğan]] sent Arrizabalaga the wrong way to put City 1–0 up. Chelsea's [[César Azpilicueta]] blasted into the top corner to level at 1–1, while [[Sergio Agüero]]'s weak effort was let in under Arrizabalaga to put City ahead 2–1.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2019/feb/24/chelsea-manchester-city-carabao-cup-match-report |title =Manchester City win Carabao Cup on penalties after Chelsea's Kepa chaos|date=24 February 2019|work=Guardian|access-date=25 February 2019}}</ref> Emerson's shot was too powerful and deflected into goal off Ederson for 2–2, and the scoreline remained as City's [[Leroy Sané]] had his penalty saved by Arrizabalaga. [[David Luiz]] failed to score for Chelsea when he hit the post, then [[Bernardo Silva]]'s effort down the middle made it 3–2 for City. Chelsea's [[Eden Hazard]] scored with the [[Panenka (penalty kick)|Panenka]] technique for 3–3, but City's [[Raheem Sterling]] scored a high shot to win the shoot-out 4–3 and crown City as champions.<ref name=telegraphlive/><ref>{{cite web |last1=Brennan |first1=Stuart |last2=Bajkowski |first2=Simon |last3=Bray |first3=Joe |title=Man City 0–0 Chelsea highlights and reaction as Raheem Sterling scores winning penalty in shoot-out |url=https://www.manchestereveningnews.co.uk/sport/football/man-city-vs-chelsea-live-15878734 |work=[[Manchester Evening News]] |access-date=25 February 2019}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=WATCH: Kepa Arrizabalaga defies furious Chelsea boss Maurizio Sarri in Carabao Cup final |url=https://news.sky.com/story/watch-kepa-arrizabalaga-defies-furious-chelsea-boss-maurizio-sarri-in-carabao-cup-final-11647428 |publisher=[[Sky News]] |access-date=25 February 2019}}</ref>

After the game, both Arrizabalaga and Sarri said that the situation was a misunderstanding with Sarri believing that Arrizabalaga was too injured with a cramp to continue, but Arrizabalaga felt well enough to do so.<ref>{{cite web |title=Maurizio Sarri: Kepa Arrizabalaga incident a 'misunderstanding', says Chelsea boss |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/47352319 |work=[[BBC News]] |access-date=25 February 2019}}</ref>
